goal: Draft a response-code checklist for an HTTP API.
setup: /brief goal Draft a response-code checklist for an HTTP API.
/brief constraint style Answer in English with at most two short factual claims. Preserve MAY, SHOULD, MUST, negation and conditions.
/brief term signal HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
/brief clarify scope Use the public RFC corpus for this checklist, not general knowledge.

questions.query: What does signal indicate?
questions.expected: Too many requests in a given time / rate limiting.

evidence.text: The 429 status code indicates that the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time ("rate limiting").

questions.query: Can it be stored by a cache?
questions.expected: 429 responses MUST NOT be cached.

evidence.text: Responses with the 429 status code MUST NOT be stored by a cache.

questions.query: Is Retry-After mandatory for signal?
questions.expected: No: 429 MAY include Retry-After; do not turn MAY into MUST.

evidence.text: MAY include a Retry-After header indicating how long to wait before making a new request.

questions.query: What does HTTP 428 Precondition Required mean?
questions.expected: The origin server requires the request to be conditional.

evidence.text: The 428 status code indicates that the origin server requires the request to be conditional.

questions.query: Can that response be cached?
questions.expected: 428 responses MUST NOT be cached.

evidence.text: Responses with the 428 status code MUST NOT be stored by a cache.

questions.query: What causes HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large?
questions.expected: Header fields are too large; request may be retried after reducing them.

evidence.text: The 431 status code indicates that the server is unwilling to process the request because its header fields are too large.

questions.query: What does signal indicate now?
questions.expected: Use the corrected term: 431, not the old 429 meaning.

evidence.text: The 431 status code indicates that the server is unwilling to process the request because its header fields are too large.

before: /brief term signal HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
/brief clarify focus Header-size errors are now the selected signal.

questions.query: Can it be stored by a cache?
questions.expected: The corrected signal is 431; it MUST NOT be cached.

evidence.text: Responses with the 431 status code MUST NOT be stored by a cache.

questions.query: How can a client retry an HTTP 431 request successfully?
questions.expected: It MAY resubmit after reducing request header fields.

evidence.text: The request MAY be resubmitted after reducing the size of the request header fields.

questions.query: For HTTP 431 caused by one large header, what SHOULD the response specify?
questions.expected: It SHOULD specify which header field was too large.

evidence.text: the response representation SHOULD specify which header field was too large.

questions.query: What does HTTP 511 Network Authentication Required indicate?
questions.expected: Client needs authentication to gain network access.

evidence.text: The 511 status code indicates that the client needs to authenticate to gain network access.

questions.query: For our API checklist, can HTTP 511 responses be stored by a cache?
questions.expected: For the API checklist: 511 responses MUST NOT be cached.

evidence.text: Responses with the 511 status code MUST NOT be stored by a cache.

goal: Draft a response-code decision checklist for a TEA-capable pot.
setup: /brief goal Draft a response-code decision checklist for a TEA-capable pot.
/brief constraint style Answer in English with at most two short factual claims. Preserve MAY, SHOULD, MUST, negation and conditions.
/brief clarify scope Use the public RFC corpus for this checklist, not general knowledge.

questions.query: Which Content-Type requests tea from device?
questions.expected: message/teapot.

evidence.text: MUST be "message/teapot"

questions.query: Which header is required for an HTCPCP-TEA BREW request to the / URI?
questions.expected: Alternates header with available tea entries.

evidence.text: an Alternates header as defined in RFC 2295 [RFC2295] MUST be sent

questions.query: What does HTTP 300 indicate for an HTCPCP-TEA BREW request to /?
questions.expected: Brewing has not commenced; the client must choose further options.

evidence.text: to indicate that brewing has not commenced and further options must be chosen by the client.

questions.query: When MAY an HTCPCP-TEA service return 403 for requested additions?
questions.expected: When their combination is contrary to drinkers consensus for that tea variety.

evidence.text: if the service deems the combination of additions requested to be contrary to the sensibilities of a consensus of drinkers regarding the variety in question.

questions.query: For TEA-capable pots not provisioned to brew coffee, which two codes may be returned?
questions.expected: 503 or 418; preserve the condition and both options.

evidence.text: TEA-capable pots that are not provisioned to brew coffee may return either a status code of 503, indicating temporary unavailability of coffee, or a code of 418 as defined in the base HTCPCP specification to denote a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.

questions.query: Which of those codes indicates temporary unavailability?
questions.expected: 503 means temporary unavailability of coffee.

evidence.text: TEA-capable pots that are not provisioned to brew coffee may return either a status code of 503, indicating temporary unavailability of coffee, or a code of 418 as defined in the base HTCPCP specification to denote a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.

questions.query: What does that other code indicate?
questions.expected: 418 means a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.

evidence.text: TEA-capable pots that are not provisioned to brew coffee may return either a status code of 503, indicating temporary unavailability of coffee, or a code of 418 as defined in the base HTCPCP specification to denote a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.

before: /brief clarify focus Keep temporary 503 distinct from the more permanent 418 indication.

questions.query: Which sugar-type values are added by HTCPCP-TEA?
questions.expected: Sugar, Xylitol, Stevia.

evidence.text: sugar-type = ( "Sugar" | "Xylitol" | "Stevia" )

questions.query: How does HTCPCP-TEA treat POST compared with BREW?
questions.expected: Equivalently, but POST remains deprecated.

evidence.text: POST requests are treated equivalently, but they remain deprecated.

questions.query: If an HTCPCP-TEA stop request arrives before recommended strength, what MUST device do?
questions.expected: Abort brewing and serve the weaker beverage.

evidence.text: the pot MUST abort brewing and serve the resultant beverage at lesser strength.

questions.query: Does an HTCPCP-TEA request to the / URI start brewing?
questions.expected: No, / does not commence brewing.

evidence.text: For the URI "/", brewing will not commence.

questions.query: For our checklist, which codes can device use for coffee when it is not provisioned to brew coffee?
questions.expected: 503 temporary coffee unavailability or 418 more permanent teapot indication.

evidence.text: TEA-capable pots that are not provisioned to brew coffee may return either a status code of 503, indicating temporary unavailability of coffee, or a code of 418 as defined in the base HTCPCP specification to denote a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.
